chapter: The Raeburn band: people and touring
title: Johnny Bothwell's deliberately corny solo
summary: Bothwell played a tasty solo on purpose to prove how corny the band's taste was.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: I remember a night, we had all been getting on Johnny Bothwell because everytime it came to a part where he had a jazz solo, he would do what I used to refer to as chicken imitations. He had a way of doing buck-buck-ba-da; I swear that's what it sounded like. His upper glisses were more chicken like than musical and a lot of the guys felt the same way I did, but we had never verbalized it. But one night we sat down with John and said, hey John, why don't you relax and just play the easy nice jazz that we know you're capable of, we heard you do it once in a while. He didn't say anything, he was deep in thought, and we wondered if he was very offended. Anyway, we let it go and we go back to the bandstand the next set and we're playing the charts and we come across one in which Johnny had his sixteen bar jazz solo; so

we get into it and he starts blowing sixteen bars, the most tasty, beautiful, ringing jazz that you could possibly hear, and we were all looking at each other, yeah, Johnny's really into it, how beautiful.

After the set we all ran over to him and instinctly everybody ran, 'yeah Johnny, babe, that's beautiful, how wonderful!' and he says, 'that goes to show you bunch of sons of bitches I purposely played as lousy as I could, just to show you how fucking corny it is.'
Can you believe that? And he was serious. He was playing lousy to show us how bad our taste was, and we thought he was playing great.
